parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is Bengali nationalism?","marks":1,"answer":"Bengali nationalism is national unity based on Bengali language, history, tradition, culture and Bengali ethnic identity.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Explain the reasons for formation of Awami Muslim League.","marks":2,"answer":"The 'Awami Muslim League' was formed due to the undemocratic and unconstitutional attitude of the Muslim League in governing the country. Since the beginning of the Pakistani regime, the Muslim League has followed policies of extreme discrimination, use of religion in politics and repression in the governance of the country. This party chose an undemocratic and unconstitutional way to run the country. A group of liberal and non-sectarian youth leaders of the Muslim League formed the 'Awami Muslim League' as a protest.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain the background of the movement that 'M' stands for.","marks":3,"answer":"The statement 'M' in the stem hints at the Language Movement of 1952. In 1947, the rulers of the newly formed Pakistan state began to discriminate against East Pakistan in various fields including political, administrative, economic, and cultural. The Pakistan government declared Urdu as the only state language of the country. This announcement angered the Bengali-speaking people of East Pakistan. A Bengali movement began with the demand to make Bengali one of the state languages. Gradually, this movement gained momentum. As a continuation of this, on February 21, 1952, students and the general public started a procession in the Dhaka University area. At one point, the police fired on the procession. As a result, Abdus Salam, Abul Barkat, Abdul Jabbar, Rafiq, and others were martyred. In exchange for their sacrifice, Bengali gained the status of one of the state languages of Pakistan in the 1956 Constitution. The statement 'M' in the stem points towards the sacrifice of the language martyrs and the achievement of the dignity of the mother tongue in exchange. In their struggle to establish Bengali as a state language, the Bengalis did not hesitate to give their lives in 1952. Therefore, it can be said that 'M' in the stem refers to the Language Movement.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Argue in favour of 'M's implied consequence of event 'N'.","marks":4,"answer":"The 'M' event of the stem that is the result of the language movement lies in the 'N' event that is 1970 election and liberation war - the comment is correct. After the formation of the state of Pakistan in 1947, the language movement was the first movement for Bengali rights. The success of this movement greatly increased the confidence of Bengalis in the struggle for rights in the state of Pakistan. It was mainly the language movement from which Bengalis began to realize that any logical and just movement can be successful if united. This attitude of Bengalis was revealed in the results of the 1970 elections. In this election, Awami League won 167 out of 169 seats in the Central Legislative Council and 298 out of 300 seats in the Provincial Council. In fact, the language movement was a movement for Bengali cultural rights. Later, this movement started the movement for economic and political rights. The success of the language movement gave inspiration to the political movement for independence in the 1960s. And along the path of the demand for autonomy comes the demand for independence. As a result, the brave Bengalis won the liberation war and brought about the birth of independent Bangladesh. In view of the above discussion, it can be said that the election of 1970 and the liberation war are the manifestations of the spirit and ideals of the language movement.\n---","image":null,"image_url":null}]
